cases.description: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars. This position is based out of the McGregor Rocket Development Facility. Travel will accompany this role, and based on business needs, opportunities to work at other SpaceX facilities may occur in the future. cases.title: Principal, Acquisitions
cases.description: You are an entrepreneurial and driven investor with impeccable values, standard-setting empathy and a high-speed mental clock; and you have consistently demonstrated that you are dedicated to making everyone around you better every day. You are committed to finding, structuring and closing the best energy investments that deliver power to large load customers including data centers. You are passionate about partnering with leading companies and other professionals to prove that sustainability can achieve market-leading returns, and your good judgment has been a key to your successes. What you will be doing at Generate Capital as a Principal, Acquisitions: - Originating energy infrastructure investment opportunities focused on powering data centers and new large loads, including behind-the-meter baseload solutions and pairing of renewables / BESS with customer load - Owning underwriting and investment execution for large load customer energy assets, including both third-party and Generate-developed opportunities, from initial diligence through investment committee and closing - Developing a differentiated market perspective by conducting market research to identify best-in-class energy developers and large load customers across priority geographies - Helping scale Generate’s in-house data center energy platform, working cross-functionally to translate large load customer energy
cases.reason: Guard for issue #3: technical origination/diligence over generation assets at an infrastructure fund stays strong — the rule targets purely financial functions only
